e: In the hope of pardon and forgiveness from his Lord, All-Hearing. Muhammad ibn Al-Jazaree Al-Shafi’ee (meaning following the Shafi’ee school of thought) says:
All Praise is due to Allah and May Allah’s Peace and Blessings be upon His Prophet ﷺ and the chosen one,
Muhammad ﷺ, his family and companions, and the reciter of Quran together with the one who is devoted to it.
And thereafter: this is an introduction concerning which the reciter of Qur’an is required to learn.
It is without any doubt required for the recitor to know before starting recitation:
The articulation points (مَخَارِج الْحُرُوْفِ) and characteristics of letters (صِفَات الْحُرُوْفِ) So that they can articulate in the most eloquent of languages.
In order to make clear the application of tajweed and the stops and that which is written in the (‘Uthmani) copies of the Qur’an,
As regards to all those words that are separated and joined in it (in writing in the Qur’an), and the feminine ‘taa’ (ت) which is not written with a ‘haa’ (ة).
The articulation points of the letters are seventeen According to those who chose it by examination
The empty space in the throat and mouth has the alif and its two sisters (i.e. the wow و and yaa ي) and they are; the medd letters which stop with the (stopping of) air.
Then from the lowest part of the throat are: همزة, هاء, and from its middle then the عين, حاء

Its closest (the throat’s area closest to the mouth) are: غين and خاء. And the قاف: the deepest part of the tongue above (meaning looking from the mouth inside the mouth, the قاف is deeper), then the كاف:
Lower (meaning closer to the mouth), and the middle (meaning middle of the tongue), then جيم, شين, ياء And the ضاد from its (meaning the tongue’s) side when it is close;
To the molars from its (the sides of the tongue) left or right And the لام, its (sides of the tongue) lowest part (closest to the mouth), until it (sides) ends (at the tip).

And the نون from its tip (meaning tip of the tongue) it is found under (under the لام, meaning closer to the mouth), And the راء is close to it (meaning close to the نون) it uses the top (meaning the top of the tip, with the tip).

And the طاء, دال, تاء from it (tip of the tongue from the top side) and from The upper incisors, and the whistle (meaning the letters that have the inherit characteristics of the whistle which are صاد,زاي, سين) are cozy,
from it (meaning the tip of the tongue) and above the two lower incisors. And the ظال, ذال, ثاء with the upper (the upper two front incisors),
from the edges of them both (the edges of the two from the upper incisors and the tongue); and from the inside of the lip, so the فاء with the edges of the towering incisors (front upper).
Using the lips are واو, باء, ميم

Its (the letters’) characteristics are) جهر(apparent,) رخو / رخاوة(softness, and (مستفل/ استفال) lowered Opened (منفتح, انفتاح) desisted, (مصمتة/ اصمات), and the opposite (of them) say: [The following are the opposites of these named characteristics and their letters. The first group of characteristics has the remaining letters left after the opposite characteristic’s letters are taken out.]
Its whispered (مهموس/ همس) (letters are:) “فَحَثَّهُ شَخْصٌ سَكَتْ”,
And between soft and strengthened (رخو والشديد) (are the letters:) “لِنْ عُمَرْ”
(The letters) صاد, ضاد, طاء, ظاء (have the characteristics of) مطبقة/ اطباق.
Its whistle صفير (has the letters of) صاد, زاي, سين. The ◌قَلْقَلَةٌ (has the letters) “قُطْبُ جَدٍ.” And (the letters of) softness اللين (are)
واو And ياء (that have a) sukoon and a fathah فتخة before them. And the drifting الاِنْحْرَافُ is correct,

On the لام and the را, and on it (the را, the characteristic of) repetition. And (the characteristic of) spreading (التفشي) is on the شين, and (the letter) ضاد has (the characteristic of) lengthening (استطل/استطالة).
The practical application of tajweed is without doubt compulsory Who does not read the Quran correctly is a sinner.

Because this (Qur’an) was revealed to us by Allah in this form And exactly like this (with tajweed) it reached us (from our Prophet, then related in authentic chains over generations to our present day shuyookh and those with ijaazah).
And it (tajweed) is also a beautification of recitation And an adornment of pronunciation and reading.
And it (tajweed) is giving each letter its required rights (حَقّ الْحرفِ) Of each and every characteristic as well as (giving each letter its) presented rights [or dues] (مُسْتَحَقّ الْحرفِ),
To take every one (of the letters) back to its origin (i.e. place of articulation), And to pronounce the equivalent letter in the same way (as you would pronounce that letter).
Complete (with all its characteristics) yet without any exaggeration, Being gentle in pronunciation without any abuse.
There exists nothing between (applying the التَّجْوِيْد) and leaving it, Except for a person to exercise (correctly) with his jaws.

Make attenuation (tarqeeq) “ترقيق” the letters of istifal “استفال”. And beware of making (be careful not to make) the letter alif “الألف” with velarization (tafkheem) [when it occurs after a letter of اسْتِفَال].
And the hamzah "همزة" (be careful not to give it tafkheem in): اِهْدِنَا, أَعُوْذُ, اَلْحَمْدُ اَﷲ and then the اللَّام of (likewise be careful not to give it tafkheem in): لَنَا, ﷲ,
(Also) عَلَى اﷲ, وَلْيَتَلَطَّفْ and وَلَا الضَّالِّيْنَ, And (likewise) the الْمِيْم of مَخْمَصَة and of مَرَض (be careful not to give it tafkhem),
And [be careful not to give tafkheem to] the الْبَاء of بِمْ, بَاطِل, بَرْق and بِذِيْ and take care on (observing the characteristics of) الشِّدَّة and الْجَهْر that are
In it (i.e. the الْبَاء) and in the الْجِيْم as in حُبّ الصَّبْرِ, اجْتُثَّتْ, رَبْوَة,and الْفَجْرِ,حَجّ
And make clear the letter of qalqalah "الْقَلْقَلَة" when it occurs with a sukoon (unvoweled) and when stopping on it, (meaning the qalaqalah letter) it should be even clearer (القلقلة الكبرى).
And (read with attenuation [tarqeeq]) the الْحَاء of أَحَطْتّ, حَصْحَصَ and الْحَقّ And (likewise read with attenuation [tarqeeq]) the السِيْن of يَسْطُوْنَ, مُسْتَقِيْم and يَسْقُوْنَ.
And attenuate [make tarqeeq of] the letter راء when it has a kasrah. Likewise (attenuate the راء) if it follows a letter with a kasrah when the راء has a sukoon.
If [the راء with a sukoon] it is not before a letter of الاسْتِعْلَاء Or the kasrah (before the راء with a sukoon) is not a fixed one.

There are different allowed ways (the راء having velarization or attenuation [tafkheem or tarqeeq] in the word): فِرْقٍ due to the كَسْرَة present (on the الْقَاف) And supress the (characteristic of) التَّكْرِيْر when it (the راء) occurs with a شَدَّة. اللَّامَاتِ and Other Different Rules)بَابُ اللَّامَاتِ وَأَحْكَامٍ مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ)
And make velarization [tafkheem] of the laam (اللام) in the name of اﷲ [if the laam اللام in the name اﷲ] is preceded by a fathah or a dammah as in عَبْدُ اﷲ

And velarize [make tafkheem] the letter (that has the characteristic) of الاسْتِعْلَاء and single out The (letters of) الاطباق are stronger [than the letters that have الاسْتِعْلَاء without الاطباق] like [the difference] between قَالَ and الْعَصَا.
And make obvious the [characteristic of] الإِطْبَاق of [the letter الطَّاء in]: أَحَطْتّ along with بَسَطْتّ and there is a difference of opinion (in the word) نَخْلُقْكُّمْ
Take extra caution (in order the letter does not get voweled or a qalqalah on it) on the sukoon of جَعَلْنَا, أَنْعَمْتَ,and الْمَغْضُوْب together with ضَلَلْنَا.
Make clear and obvious the (characteristic of) الانْفِتَاح of (the الذَّال of) مَحْذُوْراً [and the السِّيْن of] عَسَى out of fear of confusing it with مَحْظوْراً and عَصَى.
Observe (the characteristic of) الشِّدَّة in the الْكَاف and التَّاء As in: تَتَوَفَّىّ, شِرْكِكُمْ and فِتْنَةً.

If the first (letter) of الْمُتَمَاثِلَان [two like letters] and الْمُتَجَانِسَانِ [two similar letters] has a sukoon Then make إدغام (merge) as in: قُلْ رَّبّ and بَلْ لَّا; and make clear without any merging:

[the ياء in] فِيْ يَوْمٍ together with [the واو in] قَالُوْا وَهُمْ,[the قُلْ نَعَمْ [لام, [and also make clear with no idhgaam these letters which have close articulation points] سَبِّحْهُ, لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوْبَنَا and فَالْتَقَمَهُ. the حاء and ھاء in: الغين,سَبِّحْهُ and القاف in لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوْبَنَا, and اللام and التاء in فَالْتَقَمَهُ.

And the الضَّاد with (the characteristic of) الاسْتِطَالَة and its articulation point, is distinguished from the الظَّاء, and all of them [all the الظَّاء that occur in the Qur’an] are mentioned as follows:
In [the words] الْحِفْظ, عُظْم, الظُّهْر, ظَلّ, الظَّعْن, اللَّفْظ, ظَهْر, عَظْم, أَنْظِرْ, أَيْقَظْ,
ظَلَمَا, كَظْم, شُوَاظ, لَظَى, ظَاهِرْ, ظَمَا, اِنْتَظِرْ, ظُفْر, ظَلَام, اغْلُظْ,

ظَنّاً, أَظْفَرَ however it occurs [meaning wherever and in whatever form each of these words occur in the Qur’an, i.e. with attached pronouns],and (the word) عِظْ except, عِضِيْن, (the word) ظَلّ in سورة النَّحْل and (ظَلّ) in سورة الزُّخْرُف are the same, (meaning both written with الظَّاء)
ظَلْتُمْ, ظَلْتَ, and in سورة الرُّوْم)the word) ظَلُّوْا The same (word is found) in سورة الْحِجْر, (the word) ظَلَّتْ as well as نَظَلّ in سورة الشُّعَرَاء,
مَحْظُوْراً, يَظْلَلْنَ together with [the word] الْمُحْتَظِر, كُنْتَ فَظاّ and all [forms and derivatives of the word] النَّظَر.

Except in وَيْل (meaning هَلْ,(سورة المطففين (meaning سورة الإنسان), the first نَاضِرَة (it occurs in سورة الْقِيَامَة) the first one is read with a ضاد whereas the second is read نَاظِرَة), And (the word) الْغَيْظ not the one in سورة الرَّعْد and هُوْد is shortened (to a ضَاد),
(The word) الْحَظّ not the one in الْحَضّ عَلَى طَعَام [not the ض], and the difference (in recitation) concerning (the word) ظَنِيْن is sublime.

And when the two (letters i.e. the الضَّاد and the الظَّاء) meet it is necessary to make clear and distinct [the articulation points for both letters], [as demonstrated in the words] ◌أَنْقَضَ ظَهْرَكَ and يَعَضّ الظَّالِمُ
And in (the following words) وَعَظْتَ, اُضْطُرّ together with أَفَضْتُمْ, And distinguish the الْهْاء in جِبَاهُهُمْ and عَلَيْهِمْ.
Make clear the ghunnah of the النُّوْن and الْمِيْم when they occur with a shaddah; and read with الإِخْفَاء:
the الْمِيْم when it is has a sukoon and meets the (letter) الْبَاء according to the preferred view of the scholars [of Qur’anic recitation].

And make الإِظْهَار)meaning make the الْمِيْم clear and obvious if it follows) any of the remaining letters, (meaning all the letters except الْمِيْم and الْبَاء) and be careful not to make الإِخْفَاء (of الميم الساكنة) when it meets [is followed by] the letters الْوَاو and الْفَاء.
The rules for the التَّنْوِيْن and النُّوْن السَّاكنة consist of: الإِظْهَار (clear and obvious), الإِدْغَام (merging), الْقَلْب (change) and الإِخْفَاء (hide).

Upon meeting the letters of throat make الإِظْهَار [meaning make clear the التَّنْوِيْن and النُّوْن السَّاكِنَة]; and make الإِدْغَام [meaning merge the التَّنْوِيْن and النُّوْن السَّاكِنَة] when followed by the letters اللَّام and الرَّاء without غُنَّة [meaning nasalized sound] a required (merging).
And make الإِدْغَام (of the التَّنْوِيْن and النُّوْن السَّاكِنَة) with a غُنَّة into (the letters of the group) "يُوْمِنُ", except when within a single word as in: دُنْيَا and عَنْوَان.

الْقَلْب (which means change) is applied when it (the التَّنْوِيْن and النُّوْن السَّاكِنَة) meets the letter الْبَاء with a غُنَّة; and likewise is الإِخْفَاء (hiding) is applied with the remaining letters [meaning the letters remaining after taking out the letters of الإِظْهَار (clear and obvious), الإِدْغَام (merging), and الْقَلْب (change)].
The الْمَدّ (lengthening) occurs as لَازِم (compulsory), وَاجِب (required) And جَائِز (allowed) and both (the lengthening) and shortening have been affirmed [in the allowed or جَائِز lengthening].
The اللّازِم (compulsory) is when after a حَرْف مَدّ (medd letter) there is a سَاكِن in both states (i.e. while continuing reading or stopping) and is lengthened for six counts (الطُّوْل).

The الْوَاجِب [required lenghtening] is when it (the حَرْف الْمَدّ or medd letter) comes before a hamzah, joined (meaning a medd letter is followed immediately by a hamzah) if they are together in one word.

The الْجَائِز [allowed lengthing] is when it occurs separately (meaning when the medd letter and the hamzah meet but in two different words(. or (another type of lenghtening when) stopping on a phrase due to a temporary sukoon (مد عارض).
And after (having the knowledge of) the tajweed of the letters, It is without doubt necessary to have the knowledge of the stops
and the starts. And they (meaning the stops and starts) are thus divided into three (categories): تَامّ (complete stop/start), كَافٍ (sufficient stop/start) and حَسَن (good stop/start).

They (all three) refer to what is complete (a stop that is complete in meaning), then if there be no attachment (to what comes after it in meaning or grammar then this stop is وقف تام) or)when) there is an attachment in meaning (this type of stop is وقف كافي), then start (with what follows).

The complete التّام [stop] and الْكَافِيْ –the sufficient [stop], and in grammar [if there is an attachment to what comes after in meaning and grammar], then it is forbidden (to start with what follows), Except when stopping at the end of an aayah then it is allowed (to start with the beginning of the next ayah). For then it is الْحَسَن
That which is not complete is repulsive (قَبَيْح) [stop], And there is the compelled (or forced) stop for which the reciter should start [afterwards]with what preceded it.
There does not exist in the Qur’an a stop that is necessary nor a stop that is prohibited except for a reason (for its prohibition).

Know the الْمَقْطُوْع [those written separately as two different words]and the المَوْصُوْل [those words written as one word] and the التَاء (the female هاء which is written as ت) In the Qur’anic copy of the Imam (referring to the Uthmani script) in what follows.
Separate in ten words "أَنْ لَا" (meaning the words are written separately as two words in ten places which are): with مَلْجَأ, لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا,
تَعْبُدُوْا in سورة يَاسِيْن (aayah 70) and the second place in سورة هُوْد (aayah 26), سورة الْمُمْتَحِنَة) يُشْرِكْنَ:14), تُشْرِكْ, يَدْخُلَنّ, تَعْلُوْا عَلَى,

أن لَا يَقُوْلُوْا, لَا أَقُوْلُ; and (separate the words) "إِن مَّا" [with a kasrah on the hamzah] in سورة الرَّعْد (aayah 40), and join the "أَنْ مَا" with a فَتْحَة)on the hamzah); and (the words) “عَنْ مَا":

separate in نُهُوْا(and write separately) "مِنْ مَا" in سورة الرُّوْم:  and النِّسَاء: and there is a difference [in the copies of the Qur’an as to whether the word "مِنْ مَا" is written مقطوعة or] in سورة الْمُنَافِقِيْنَ: (and separate) " أَمْ مَنْ" in أَسَّسَ(as well as in)

سورة فًصِّلَتْ (aayah 40), سورة النِّسَاء (aaayah 109) and الذِّبْح (i.e. سورة الصَّافَّات aayah 11), (and separate) "حَيْثُ مَا", "أَنْ لَمْ" with a فَتْحَة (on the hamzah), and (write separate) "إِنّ مَا" with the كَسْرَة (on the hamzah)
In سورة الأَنْعَام (aayah 134) and (separate)"أَنّ مَا" with the فَتْحَة (on the hamzah) in يَدْعُوْنَ both of them; It differs in سورة الأنفال:  and سورة النَّحْل:.

And [separate in writing] "كُلّ مَا" in سَأَلْتُمُوهُand it differs in رُدُّوْا and likewise (there is a difference as regards to the words) بِئْسَ مَا in قُلْ بِئْسَمَا and (the places where the words"بِئْس مَا" are written) joined are as follows:
◌خَلَفْتُمُوْنِيْ and اشْتَرَوْا. Separate (the words) "فِيْ مَا" in أُوْحِيَ, أَفَضْتُمْ, in  اشْتَهَتْ and both لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ",
The second فَعَلْنَ, also in سورة الْوَاقِعَة) وَقَعَتْ:61), in سورة الرُّوْم:, both places in سورة الزُّمَر) تَنْزِيْل:30) and in سورة الشُّعَرَاء: 147 and join what is besides these (occurrences).
Join "أَيْنَما" as in سورة النَّحْل: (join as well) and there is a difference (in the copies of the Quran) described in سورة الشُّعَرَاء:, سورة الأَحْزَاب: and سورة النِّسَاء:.
Join "إِلَّمْ" in سورة هُوْد (aayah 14), أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ, نَجْمَعَ, (also join) تَحْزَنُوْا: لِكَيْلَا, تَأْسَوْا عَلَى
As well as [كَيْلَا]in سورة الْحَجّ, in عَلَيْكَ حَرَجٌ. And separate [in writing] "عَنْ مَنْ" in يَشَاءُ, عَنْ مَنْ) مَنْ تَوَلَّىَ in سورة النَّجْم:29) and (separate) "يَوْمَ هُمْ".

(And write separately the words) "مَالِ هَذَا", (مَالِ الَّذِيْنَ) الَّذِيْنَ and (مَالِ هَؤُلَاءِ) هَؤُلَاءِ  (The word) “ولات حين” is forbidden to pronounce according to the Imam as joined into one word.
Join (the words in writing) “وَزَنُوْهُمْ” and “كَالُوْهُمْ” And similarly (join)"يَا", "أَلْ" and"هَا" do not separate (these from what comes after).

(The word) “رَحْمَت” in سورة الزُّخْرُف (two places) is written [in the Uthmani script] with an open تَاء (meaning "ت" and not with a هَاء like "ة / ة") (and likewise in) سورة الأَعْرَاف:, سورة الرُّوْم:, سورة هُوْد:, سورة مريم) كَاف:2) and سورة الْبَقَرَة:217.

(Also written with a تَاء is the word) is "نِعْمَت" and the last three (places) in سورة النَّحْل:,, 114 and the last two (places) in سورة إبراهيم:,. and the second (place) in الْعُقُوْد (i.e. سورة الْمَائِدَة:, where it is mentioned with the word) "هَمّ"

(Likewise the word "نِعْمَت") in سورة لُقْمَان:, then in سورة فَاطِر: as is the case with سورة الطُّوْر:; and سورة آل عِمْرَان: 103 and (also written with a لَعْنَت" (تَاء" in it (meaning سورة آل عِمْرَان:61) and in سورة النُّوْر:

And (also written with a امْرَأَت" (تَاء" in سورة يُوْسُف (in two places aayah 30 and 51), سورة آل عِمْرَان:, سورة الْقَصَص: and سورة التَّحْرِيْم (in three places in aayah 10 and 11), And (also written with a مَعْصِيَتْ" (تَاء" in سورة المجادلة: and.
And (also written with a شَجَرَت" (تَاء" in سورة الدُّخَان:, all (of the words) "سُنَّت" in سورة فَاطِر, (aayah 58) of سورة الأَنْفَال and the last (occurrence) in سورة غَافِر:.
And (also written with a قُرَّت عَيْنٍ" (تَاء"and "جَنَّت" in وَقَعَتْ (i.e. سورة الْوَاقِعَة:87), "فِطْرَتْ", "بَقِيَّت", "ابْنَت"  and "كَلِمَتْ"
In the middle of سورة الأَعْرَاف (aayah 137), and all that on which there is difference (in the copies of the Qur’an) in terms of being plural or singular is known to be (written) with a تَاء.
Start on the hamzah al-wasl (at the beginning of a verb) with a ضَمَّة if the third letter of the verb has a a ضَمَّة

And (start the هَمْزَة وَصْلٍ) with a kasrah (when the third letter of the verb has) a كَسْرَة or فَتْحَة. and in the الأَسْمْاء (i.e. nouns) other than the اللَّام (i.e. other than those starting with the definite article "أَلْ") start it (the hamzah al-wasl) with a kasrah, and in:
(and start the irregular nouns also with a كَسْرَة and they are:) ابْن, together with ابْنَة, امْرِئ, اثْنَيْنِ, اسْم, امْرَأَة together with اثْنَتَيْنِ.
Beware of stopping with a full vowel except if you are applying الرَّوْم then (pronounce) a portion of the vowel

Except (meaning you are not allowed to stop with الرَّوْم) on the فَتْحَة or its مَنْصُوْب; and apply الإِ◌شْمْام [by] showing a ضَمَّة (of the lips) in the case of (the last letter having a) الرَّفْع or ضَّمَّة.
My poem of this introduction has come to an end from me to the recitor of the Quran I give (this poem) as a present.
Its verses are قَاف (i.e. a hundred) and زَاي (i.e. seven) in number, whosoever beautifies recitation with التَّجْوِيْد will truly gain true guidance.
“All Praise is due to Allah” for the conclusion to it (this poem) as well And thereafter the peace and blessings be:
On the chosen Prophet ﷺ, his family, and his companions, and those who follow his example.
